summary: This note describes how cake became a mass-produced product during the Great Depression. A surplus of molasses and the need to feed economically depressed Americans led one company to patent a cake-bread mix, establishing the first cake-in-a-box line. As a result, cake shifted from a home- or bakery-made specialty to a mass-produced good.
one_line: How the Great Depression-era molasses surplus and a patented cake-bread mix launched the first cake-in-a-box product.
key_facts: During the Great Depression, there was a surplus of molasses in the United States.
There was a need to provide easily made food to millions of economically depressed people in the United States during the Great Depression.
One company patented a cake-bread mix to deal with the Depression-era economic situation.
The patented cake-bread mix established the first line of cake in a box.
Cake as it is known today became a mass-produced good as a result of the cake-in-a-box line.
Before this shift, cake was largely a home-made or bakery-made specialty.
The note does not name the company that patented the cake-bread mix.
The note does not give a specific date for the patent or the first cake-in-a-box line.
